_evidence: MEASURED (safetensors headers read directly from BOTH the packed-U8 checkpoint AND the expanded-bf16 checkpoint on disk -- every number below is an exact tensor-shape/dtype computation, not a formula guess). Zero mlx/torch load, zero HCLI resident contention.
_label: Odyssey I DISCOVERY + a direct Byte Elimination Law comparison point: this specimen was NATIVELY trained at extreme low precision, not Gravity-compressed by Hawking. What does its REAL complete-system EBPW look like under Hawking's own accounting discipline?

native_packing_CONFIRMED_from_header_com.mechanism: linear-layer weight matrices are packed 4 ternary values per U8 byte (confirmed by comparing the SAME tensor's shape in both checkpoints: bf16 first-dim is exactly 4x the packed U8 first-dim). Each packed matrix carries ONE extra BF16 'weight_scale' scalar (shape=[1]) -- a single global scale per matrix, negligible overhead.
native_packing_CONFIRMED_from_header_com.ternary_weight_only_bpw_note: EXACTLY 2.0 bits/weight, not the '1.58' in the model's own name -- 1.58 bits is the theoretical entropy of a 3-state {-1,0,+1} symbol (log2(3)=1.585); the ACTUAL on-disk packing achieves 2.0 bits/weight (4-per-byte), a real, measured, honest gap between theoretical minimum and shipped packing efficiency.

COMPLETE_SYSTEM_EBPW_the_real_finding.finding: 86.37% of parameters ARE the packed ternary linear weights (2.0 bpw each), but the remaining 13.63% (token embeddings, all norms, per-matrix scale scalars) stay FULL BF16 (16 bits) and are NOT quantized at all. Because that BF16 remainder still commands a large share of total STORAGE BYTES (even at 13.63% of PARAMS, at 8x the per-param cost of the ternary weights), the COMPLETE payload-accounted EBPW is 3.9077 bits/weight -- 1.95x the ternary-only figure, and 2.47x the model's own '1.58-bit' name. This is EXACTLY the 'no fake sub-bit accounting' trap the Byte Elimination Law warns about: the correct, complete-system EBPW for this NATIVELY-ternary, production-shipped model is ~3.9 bpw, not ~1.6 or even 2.0 -- a real external benchmark for where Hawking's own Gravity ladder (<2.5->2.0->1.5->1.0) stands relative to a real, capability-verified (per the model card) production system.

obvious_representation_opportunities: The embedding table + norms (13.63% of params, staying full BF16) are the DOMINANT contributor to the gap between 2.0 and 3.9 complete_bpw. This session's O006 finding (protect non-expert organs, push the dominant redundant organ aggressively) does NOT directly apply here -- BitNet already pushed its DOMINANT organ (linear weights, 86% of params) to the extreme; the remaining lever is whether the EMBEDDING TABLE SPECIFICALLY (vocab_size=128256 x hidden_size, likely the single largest BF16 tensor) could itself tolerate a more aggressive codec without the same complexity-reduction logic that protects small norm vectors -- untested, a real next question.
failure_modes_not_yet_tested: No Doctor capability battery -- the model card claims parity with similar-size full-precision models, not independently verified here.
preliminary_disposition: RESEARCH SPECIMEN / EXTERNAL BENCHMARK. A real, production, natively-ternary model gives Hawking's own EBPW ladder a genuine outside reference point: 3.91 complete_bpw is where a serious production system with deliberate low-bit design actually lands once embeddings/norms are honestly counted -- useful context for judging how aggressive <=1.5/<=1.0 GRAVITY QUALIFIED targets really are.

preliminary_star_resident_evaluation.resident_candidate: PLAUSIBLE ON SIZE: 2.41B params, 1.18GB packed footprint -- one of the smallest specimens surveyed this session. max_position_embeddings=4096 is short but not as constraining as mamba3-siso's 2048. Genuinely worth a capability battery.
preliminary_star_resident_evaluation.verdict: WORTH A CAPABILITY BATTERY -- small, natively efficient, real production release with a documented eval suite (per its own model card, not independently reproduced here).
